A column of ring marks runs down the left margin of every page (the 'watermark bar'); it carries no content. Instructions (iii)-(vii) confirm full80 (38 q / 80 marks). Instruction (viii) prints 2 internal choices in B, 2 in C, 2 in D and 3 in E: Q21, Q24, Q27, Q29, Q34, Q35, Q36, Q37, Q38, each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper AND a bare OR in the 30/2/3 marking scheme (9 in both; Q22, Q23, Q25, Q26, Q28, Q30-33 carry none). Section-A keys read off the 30/2/3 marking scheme (ms idx 2-8) as images and each re-derived: all 20 agree. No void or 'full marks to every attempt' note anywhere in the scheme. Decimal points are ORDINARY full stops (Q16 2.5/7.5, Q32 1.732, Q33 5.6/20.0, Q37 18.5), checked at full size. No 'Case Study - N' headings printed, so no _caseStudyLabel. Sibling of 2024-30-2-1: 40 rows are the reference's questions (confirmed on this paper's pages, stem/context/options/answer/chapter/subtopic/difficulty copied byte-for-byte, figures re-read on this paper); 11 rows transcribed fresh (Q1, Q8, Q9, Q12, Q23, Q25, Q26, Q30, Q32, Q35a, Q35b). Case studies are reordered against 30/2/1: Q36 here is its Q38 (pie chart), Q37 its Q37 (circus), Q38 its Q36 (ball).

questions.subtopic: Trigonometric Identities
questions.context: Directions : In Question 19 and 20, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given. Select the correct option from the following :
questions.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** If \(\sin A = \dfrac{1}{3}\) \((0^\circ < A < 90^\circ)\), then the value of \(\cos A\) is \(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\)

**Reason (R) :** For every angle \(\theta\), \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\).

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true. Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true. Reason (R) does not give correct explanation of (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is not true.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is not true but Reason (R) is true.
